title: PXAPI problem v1
description: A transport-neutral, client-readable description of why an operation did not succeed. It carries no HTTP status, no type URI and no other transport binding; the adapter that owns a transport maps this document onto it. Every text member is single-line, bounded and produced from a fixed template, and every validation error is reported structurally as a JSON pointer plus the violated schema keyword, so that validator free text, exception messages, tracebacks, filesystem paths, tokens and secrets cannot appear here by construction.

schema_version.description: Required. Always 1.0.0 for this contract. Each contract is versioned in its own right; this value is not a version of the contract set as a whole.

code.description: Required. A stable machine-readable problem code. The codes known at this contract version are listed in the registry manifest; the set is open, and a client must handle a code it does not know as a generic problem of the given title and detail.

title.description: Required. A short human-readable summary that is the same for every occurrence of the code. It is a fixed string per code, never per-occurrence text.

detail.description: Required. A bounded explanation of this occurrence, rendered from a fixed template and values the producer resolved from its own registry. Never validator free text, never an exception message, never a path.

run_id.description: Optional. The Analysis Run the problem is attributable to. Absent means the problem is not attributable to a run, for example because the request never became one.

pointer.description: Required. An RFC 6901 JSON pointer to the offending location in the submitted document; the empty string is the document root.

keyword.description: Required. The JSON Schema keyword that was violated, for example required, const, pattern or additionalProperties. Pointer and keyword together are enough for a client to locate and understand the violation without any prose.

errors.description: Required. The individual violations for a validation problem, empty for a problem that is not about a document. The collection is finitely bounded: a producer reports at most maxItems entries and states the untruncated violation count in detail, so a pathological document cannot turn one problem into an unbounded response.
